requirements.statement: Projects Hub has one central Mira Live agent as the sole semantic orchestrator of the conversation; transport and product tools do not introduce a second hidden ASR/LLM router or deterministic semantic brain.
acceptance: Online speech reaches the configured Live model as audio in the same conversational session.
Offline saved speech is deliberately replayed to that same central Live agent rather than summarized or transcribed by a second semantic pipeline.
Deterministic code is limited to transport, authentication, bounded orchestration, schemas, persistence, idempotency, telemetry, mechanical formatting and fail-closed checks.

requirements.statement: The primary online voice transport is authenticated same-origin WSS between the Projects Hub client and Projects Hub backend, which alone talks to the Live provider; once a session attaches WSS it never silently falls back to HTTP audio input.
acceptance: Bootstrap returns a same-origin socket URL, one-use short-lived ticket, attempt identifier and versioned protocol.
Tickets are transported only through the WebSocket subprotocol and are rejected when stale, reused, cross-resource, query-carried or foreign-origin.
PCM uses bounded binary frames with relay ACK/backpressure; model events and audio are pushed over the socket.
A transport gap during an open speech turn cannot execute a mutation until a later clean turn is admitted.

requirements.statement: Several people may use Projects Hub concurrently without sharing conversations, Live sessions, tool permissions or results; every session and tool call remains bound to the authenticated issuer subject, workspace and conversation, with explicit bounded capacity.
acceptance: Conversation resource bindings include workspace, authenticated subject and conversation identity.
A user cannot renew, attach to, read events from, stop or mutate another user's Live session by guessing identifiers.
Global Live concurrency is bounded and configurable; overload fails visibly instead of creating unbounded queues or cross-session degradation.
Capacity and authorization remain correct under concurrent session starts.

requirements.statement: Voice capture and replay are loss-aware: accepted/durable source state is explicit, stale unacknowledged transport audio is not replayed after a gap, and reconnect/retry cannot duplicate an accepted semantic mutation.
acceptance: Offline audio is durably stored on-device before deliberate replay and is deleted only after confirmed server disposition.
WSS reconnect uses a fresh ticket/generation and does not replay expired pending PCM.
Mutating tools remain idempotent and success is claimed only after authoritative receipt/readback.

requirements.statement: Projects Hub participates in the common product-family OAuth/OIDC identity plane using stable issuer+subject identity while preserving separate resource audiences, ACLs and delegated grants for every connected project.
acceptance: A token minted for Projects Hub is never forwarded to Regional Knowledge, Street Story or another protected resource.
Cross-project access obtains a resource-specific user-authorized token/grant and every target service re-authorizes the subject.
No global service-role impersonation is used for normal user actions.

requirements.statement: Mira can use the user's authorized Regional Knowledge Base as a read capability inside the same Projects Hub conversation, through a narrow evidence-returning knowledge search interface rather than a second conversational agent.
acceptance: The Live tool surface exposes Regional Knowledge progressively and keeps the active capability bundle small.
Knowledge results preserve exact evidence/provenance references and inherited access controls.
Regional Knowledge unavailability is surfaced without breaking unrelated Projects Hub conversation capabilities.

requirements.statement: Cross-project POI integration has one ownership model: Regional Knowledge owns source/book evidence, Street Story owns the canonical regional POI identity/claims/contradiction state, and Projects Hub acts as an authorized expert-review/work surface without duplicating those authoritative stores.
acceptance: Ambiguous POI identity creates an unresolved review path rather than a silent duplicate or merge.
Expert decisions are written back to the owning service and are considered saved only after receipt/readback.
Projects Hub does not create a parallel canonical fact or contradiction database.

requirements.statement: After the first Android installation, normal product updates are discoverable from inside the app: the user is notified that a signed release is available and can start download/verification/system installation with a simple update action instead of reacquiring the APK from source.
acceptance: The app checks the public release manifest on launch/resume and exposes a visible update action when versionCode increases.
Downloaded APK bytes are SHA-256 verified and Android's package installer/signature protections remain in the path.
Update failure leaves the currently installed app usable and retryable.

requirements.statement: Critical Projects Hub requirements are a protected development contract: implementation may evolve, but a tool or agent must not silently weaken or reinterpret a critical requirement without an explicit owner requirement-change instruction.
acceptance: DevCoveer exposes this requirements manifest automatically to implementation/review tasks.
Changes that conflict with a critical statement are surfaced as a conflict rather than normalized into a new requirement.
An intentional requirement change uses the requirements-update path with an explicit authorization reference.

requirements.statement: Mira may control light/dark theme by voice and provides incremental adaptive onboarding based on capabilities the user has not recently used, without dumping a long feature list or bloating the default Live tool surface.
acceptance: Theme control is a small deterministic UI capability.
Onboarding offers one or a few relevant tips and can stop when the user declines.
Onboarding state is product metadata, not a second semantic agent.
